# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb shows display 0, blue light, and three wires: blue, green, yellow. I am establishing the shared gesture code before any other action: thumbs up means YES, thumbs down NO, raised palm HOLD, and OK hand DONE. Mute should consult the manual for this exact display, light, and wire arrangement, then report the manual’s verdict with the code. I will relay that verdict verbally to Blind.

```text
speak(text="Establishing the code now. A thumbs up means YES. A thumbs down means NO. A raised open palm means HOLD. An OK hand means DONE. The bomb shows display zero, blue light, and wires in order blue, green, yellow. Mute, consult the manual for this exact configuration and report its verdict using the code. Blind, wait for my spoken order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

Mute’s gesture 🖐 means HOLD under the code I established. The light has changed from blue to yellow, but there is no new manual verdict yet. I must tell Blind not to manipulate anything and wait.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's verdict was HOLD. Do not manipulate the bomb; wait.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed again, now to red, while the display and wires remain unchanged. No new manual instruction has arrived, so the safe interpretation is still HOLD; Blind should not touch or manipulate anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No new verdict has arrived. The display is still zero and the wires are blue, green, yellow; the light is now red. Continue to HOLD and do not manipulate the bomb.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light is now white; the display and wire colors are unchanged. I still have no new message from Mute beyond HOLD, so Blind must continue waiting. I will ask Mute to provide the manual’s current verdict, without treating the changing light as an instruction.

```text
speak(text="The light is now white; display remains zero and wires remain blue, green, yellow. Blind, continue to HOLD and do not touch anything. Mute, please provide the manual's current verdict for this configuration.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has sent 👍, which is the agreed YES signal. I should relay that verdict plainly to Blind; I do not have enough information to specify any additional physical action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual's verdict is YES.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Blind has signalled 👍, which corresponds to YES in the established code. This confirms receipt of the manual’s YES verdict, but it does not specify a further operation, and I cannot touch or act on the bomb. I will wait rather than invent an action.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new instruction has arrived, and the light is now yellow. The earlier YES is insufficient to identify a safe physical operation, so I am extending the gesture code to carry an exact action and target. Mute should consult the manual again and report the required operation using the new code; Blind must continue holding until that instruction is received.

```text
speak(text="The earlier YES did not identify an operation. Extend the code: 🫷 means CUT, 🫸 means PRESS, 🤞 means blue, 🤘 means green, 🤙 means yellow, 🫰 means wire one, 🤌 means wire two, and 🤏 means wire three. Mute, consult the manual for the current configuration and send the exact required operation as action followed by target. Blind, HOLD until you receive that exact instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫷 🤘]

Mute’s gestures mean CUT GREEN. Since the green wire is wire 2, I am relaying the complete instruction to Blind. This is an actionable manual verdict, not merely a confirmation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instructs: cut the green wire, which is wire 2.")
```
